Perhaps you have been lucky. Maybe you had friends that shared your own interests, people you liked to spend time with. But not everyone is so lucky.

When i was a kid no one of my peers shared my interests, i disliked spending time with them because they never did anything interesting. So i used to spend my time alone inside (when not in school). Yes, i did go out with my bike from time to time, i did try to socialize... but they just weren't like me, and they knew it too. To them i was just "weird" and they treated me consequently. I was interested in science, chemistry, electronics, computers... no one of them did care about these things.

To me, my computer was my best friend and i spent with it most of my childhood, and i am very thankful i had it because it made my life interesting even if no one around me (adults included) did even understand the things i liked.

Back in those days computers were pretty much a new thing, i think i was one of the first (if not the first) to have one in my house in my village. Internet did not exist and i didn't even know what a BBS was... so i was pretty much all by myself with my manuals, books and so on. No one to share my little discoveries, no one to talk about it all, no one to even share my happiness or my frustration when i could or could not accomplish something.

I wish i had a friend that could understand, kid or adult, even a virtual/online one would have been great. But without Internet (or BBSes) that was just impossible.

I was very lonely of course... the only friend i had that could understand was my middle-school's math teacher and i spent a lot of time with him... but only during school time. I also had a little cousin that was interested in what i liked (i think i have infected him)... but he lived far away, he also was much younger than me and we only got to see each other like once per month.

I would have literally killed to have someone to talk to about the things that mattered to me, someone to discover the things together, someone that could teach me or that i could teach to, someone that could learn with me.

If you are born in a little village you just don't have many chances to find someone that shares your interests and someone you like to spend your time with.

So, to some people an online friend is really, really helpful and important. Yes, you do miss physical contact, we are human beings after all, but having someone to talk to is still much better than nothing, believe me. You look at that picture and it makes you sad... i look at it and i think "kids today are lucky".

I will love when VR is realistic enough to make us feel like it's real but at the same time I know sad things like this will happen. But if someone lonely could be made to feel loved, even virtually, I think it's a good thing.
